evidence: M1-T11: patch changes only the provider dependency hash; its own context, task, edges, architecture, definition and effective paths match the recorded baseline. DSH model/path rules are now explicit; dispatch still consumes immutable launch snapshots (packages/daemon/src/service/dispatch.ts:656,2411) and default adapter at packages/daemon/src/boot/container.ts:520. No task status or historical batch verdict changed.

Changed provider contract: current DSH native service probe + smoke returned isAvailable=true/canDispatch=true for 0.2.0-rc.2; adapter-built real headless task returned DSH_SCHEDULER_FIXED_OK, exit 0, empty stderr. Existing streaming/reply/resume/model-rejection capability bits remain unchanged. Focused provider tests 110 passed/1 existing Windows skip; registry/routes/argument guards 24 passed.

Terminal syntax: six JSON-looking object/array answer cases failed before repair (missing or extracted content). Full answers are now preserved as text exactly once. Native stderr separation: a real Node subprocess and four production-container cases failed before repair because diagnostics were mixed into stdout/assistant events; native collection and text attachment now use stdout-only onLine, while raw logs retain stderr. Current installed headless streams dsh: reasoning: to stderr on successful runs; its documented progress block is accepted, while other diagnostics, nonzero exit and empty final stdout remain rejected. Six new stderr regressions failed before repair and pass after repair. Latest affected suite: 17 files/311 tests passed; TypeScript/Biome passed. A real local DSH JSON task returned {status:DSH_NATIVE_JSON_OK}, exit 0, and current service returned isAvailable/canDispatch true. The first native JSON task also exited 0 with the correct answer but triggered the old test assertion because reasoning was present; its captured stdout mixing and native headless source identify the corrected contract. No existing live UI recovery claim is made.

Production composition: container-wiring.test.ts:549 drives the real container/default adapter/run service from DSH plain stdout through initial review and a new review session. It failed first because stdout produced no normalized content, then because review received bare dsh; enabling stdout-only acceptsPlainText for DSH and injecting agentService into createReviewService made it pass. Full affected suite: 17 files/311 tests passed; TypeScript and changed-file Biome passed. These integration tests use a controlled subprocess and are not a live browser/native-provider bootstrap claim.

Discovered-executable regression: manual createRun and scheduler tick failed before repair because their snapshots contained bare dsh; both now freeze the probe-resolved path and the real default DSH adapter receives that path. Changing availability after snapshot creation does not replace the saved executable. DSH review builder also honors the supplied path (failed before, passed after). Focused dispatch/review/desktop tests 51 passed; all affected review/wrapup/bughunt/container stages 139 passed, TypeScript and changed-file Biome passed.

Consumer verification: dispatch-spawn, container-wiring and agents-models-login integration tests 46 passed; DSH review-launch plus current desktop CLI tests 25 passed. Review keeps read-only permissions, inherits the native model when null and rejects explicit unsupported model overrides.

Startup/report regression: production-container model override previously left its run in starting; now launch construction is inside the existing startup failure handler and the run reaches failed, task lane is null and no process spawns. Five terminal output cases previously lost line separators; stdout normalization now preserves separators, including multiline headers and JSON forms, and emits only once. Both regressions fail before and pass after repair. Final full affected suite: 17 files/313 tests passed with no unhandled errors, TypeScript and changed-file Biome passed. A scope error in the intermediate guard move was caught by TypeScript and the affected suite, then corrected by retaining LaunchSpec for the Codex session; final checks cover the existing Codex composition too.

Blank terminal lines: the stable production-container regression failed before repair because normalized text lost blank separators; after repair, complete concatenated stdout retains middle/leading/trailing blank lines. Whitespace-only stdout is a negative content control and still enters awaiting_human without spawning a review. Initial output assertions could race asynchronous event persistence, so they now wait for the complete concatenated terminal text rather than the first event. Mapping blank lines initially made the content counter true; delaying leading whitespace until nonblank content fixed this and the negative control passes. Final affected suite: 17 files/316 tests passed, no unhandled errors; TypeScript and changed-file Biome passed. Contract hash and support paths are unchanged.

Review output/startup regressions: before repair, 10 DSH cases failed: stderr VERDICT pass was accepted despite empty or malformed stdout; mixed stderr broke seven valid final verdict controls; rejecting a persisted model left the next review starting. Initial and new-session DSH reviews now attach stdout-only terminal mapping; DSH finalizeReview forbids mixed raw fallback even when no content was emitted. New-session review attaches output/exit supervision and transitions to running; launch rejection uses the existing failed/awaiting_human recovery path. Seven complete terminal controls now finish both review rounds with persisted pass verdict; two stderr-only controls persist incomplete, and model-rejection row reaches failed without spawning. Focused 12 passed; full affected suite 17 files/319 tests passed with no unhandled errors. TypeScript and changed-file Biome passed. These are real production-container services with controlled subprocesses, not live UI acceptance. The only new effective path is review-round.test.ts; no task requirement is relaxed.

Changed AC1/E-193: build-launch-spec.ts:34/config/defaults.ts:276 inherit the DSH configured model and use a discoverable dsh command; platform/windows.ts:116-125 finds packaged Windows launchers. Explicit JS paths remain supported by launch construction. Explicit model selection is rejected rather than ignored or passed as unsupported --model.
